baselineDisplay.title: Australian Aboriginal Rock Art
baselineDisplay.text:
Australian Aboriginal rock art is among the most highly prized in the world, thanks to its age, detail, freshness, and range of colour. Australia is estimated to have as many as 100,000 rock art sites. In many areas it’s possible to visit this rock art accompanied by an Aboriginal person who can provide explanations and cultural interpretations of each work’s complicated meaning. A painted rock fragment from Nawarla Gabarnmang has been estimated to be about 28,000 years old. Some sites are among the oldest in the world, estimated to be 40,000 years old.
The rock art is also a record of Aboriginal life many centuries ago. You can admire ancient figures carrying spears, boomerangs, bows and arrows, frogs and other animals, a sailing ship, and a female spirit with four arms.
